Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. You may also be eligible for the Rodzina 800+ benefit, which provides PLN 800 per child per month for dependents under temporary protection, potentially improving your financial situation during retirement planning [S1][S102].

2) Quick budget check: Your monthly income is PLN 5510.0, and your total monthly expenses are PLN 5100.0, leaving you with a surplus of PLN 410.0.

Maintain a monthly saving plan of around PLN 400-500 to supplement your retirement income, adjusting as your budget allows (general rule of thumb, not Poland-specific). [S100] 4. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension.
