Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Given your medium priority for retirement and family responsibilities, a realistic initial target is to save around PLN 400-600 monthly towards retirement, balancing essential expenses and healthcare needs (general rule of thumb, not Poland-specific). Additionally, as a resident with dependents, you may be eligible for the Rodzina 800+ benefit, which provides PLN 800 per child per month, potentially adding PLN 1600 monthly to your family income and improving your financial stability.

2) Quick budget check: Your monthly income is PLN 7450.0, and your total monthly expenses are PLN 6840.0, leaving you with a surplus of PLN 610.0.

3) Suggested monthly retirement saving amount: PLN 400-600 per month (general rule of thumb, not Poland-specific)

Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension.
