Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. In Poland, the statutory retirement age is 65 for men, and old-age pensions depend on the contributions paid to the Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) and the length of your insurance period [S2][S102]. Since you are not sure if you are registered with ZUS or making social security contributions, it is crucial to start or verify your registration to build your pension rights. The minimum old-age pension amount is around PLN 1,780.96 gross per month as of 2024, but this can vary, so checking the current amount on the official ZUS website is recommended [S1].

2) Quick budget check: Your monthly income is PLN 5850.0, and your total monthly expenses are PLN 5590.0, leaving you with a surplus of PLN 260.0.

3) Suggested monthly retirement saving amount: PLN 200-260 per month, adjusting as your budget allows (general rule of thumb, not Poland-specific).

4) Retirement-related options in Poland: Register with ZUS and start making compulsory old-age pension contributions to build your pension rights [S2].; Use the ZUS online calculator to check your projected pension based on your contribution history and plan accordingly [S100][S101].; Consider voluntary ZUS contributions if you have gaps in your contribution history or are self-employed to increase your future pension [S2].; Apply for old-age pension upon reaching the statutory retirement age of 65 for men, ensuring you meet the required insurance period [S102].

5) Next steps: 1. Confirm your current registration status with ZUS by logging into the PUE ZUS platform or contacting ZUS directly [S100]. 2. If not registered, register with ZUS to start making social security contributions, focusing on old-age pension insurance [S2]. 3. Use the ZUS pension calculator online to estimate your future pension and adjust your savings plan accordingly [S100][S101]. 4. Review your monthly expenses to identify small savings opportunities, such as optimizing utilities or reducing discretionary spending, to increase your retirement savings gradually. 5. Keep track of your contribution history regularly to avoid gaps and ensure continuous pension rights accumulation.

6) Sources used: [S1], [S2], [S100], [S101], [S102]

Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. Contents of https://www.gov.pl/web/your-europe/old-age-pension--step-by-step: Old-age pension – step by step - Your Europe in Poland - Gov.pl website Back ## Old-age pension – step by step An old-age pension is a cash benefit paid from the Social Insurance Fund to persons who decide to exit the labour market after reaching retirement age. The purpose of the benefit is to provide an income in retirement. Old-age pensions are granted upon application or – in certain situations – ex officio. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension. A right, not an obligation Retirement is a right, not an obligation. After reaching statutory retirement age, a person may decide whether to exercise this right straight away or at a later date if they wish to remain on the labour market. Importantly, the later you retire, the higher your old-age pension will be. This is because the amount of an old-age pension depends on the sum of pension contributions paid, the amount of initial capital, the amount of funds accumulated in a sub-account and life expectancy. When can a person retire? After reaching statutory retirement age. Since 1 October 2017, the general retirement age has been 60 years for women and 65 years for men. After reaching this age, men and women may decide whether they wish to continue to work or leave work and retire. Apart from reaching the general retirement age, a person must also document that they have completed a period of insurance and terminate their employment relationship in order to receive an old-age pension.
